impl:v01-feed-no-sorter.change_summary: app.rb: the FEED statement drops the `ORDER BY created_at DESC,id DESC` inside group_concat and the now-unused `,p.created_at,p.id` projection of the 20-row subquery; the subquery's own `ORDER BY p.created_at DESC,p.id DESC LIMIT 20` is kept and still runs as a co-routine over posts_created_at_id_idx, so the aggregate consumes rows already in order and SQLite no longer builds a temp b-tree per feed (EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN: `USE TEMP B-TREE FOR group_concat(ORDER BY)` gone, same plan otherwise). The old text is kept as FEED_SORTED and a private Store#feed_sql guard runs once at boot, before `@feed = @db.prepare_splat(...)` (so before warm-up and listen): it checks `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN FEED` for "TEMP B-TREE" and compares `@db.query_single_splat(FEED)` with `@db.query_single_splat(FEED_SORTED)`; on either failure it warns with a distinct message ("feed plan uses a sorter" / "feed plan drift") and prepares FEED_SORTED instead (fail-safe per the tech vetting; both boot documents are discarded, nothing stored in an ivar). README.md documents the optimization, the dependency on the pinned SQLite 3.54.0 co-routine delivery order and the boot-time enforcement. Nothing else changed (no Gemfile/pragmas/sqlite_train.c/install.sh edits).
impl:v01-feed-no-sorter.hand_tests: All run against tdsc-cicloid:v01-feed-no-sorter started like run.sh (seccomp unconfined, nofile 65535, seed/feed.db copied to /tmp/feed.db). (1) Boot log of the server: only the IO::Buffer warning and "listening on 0.0.0.0:3000 (142 iseqs compiled)"; no "feed plan" warning, so the sorter-free FEED is the prepared statement. (2) SQLite-level verify script (bundle exec ruby in the image, scratch copy of seed DB, SQLite 3.54.0): EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN old text has `USE TEMP B-TREE FOR group_concat(ORDER BY)`, new text has none, otherwise identical CO-ROUTINE / SCAN posts_created_at_id_idx / SEARCH u / covering likes_post_id_idx plan; old vs new documents byte-identical on seed (5102 B), after 100/200/300/400/500 mixed likes+creates, with 25 extra posts sharing the same created_at (id DESC tie-break), and `{"posts":[]}` on an empty schema; `db.respond_to?(:query_single_value) == false` confirmed (hence query_single_splat). (3) End-to-end over HTTP with seed/tokens.json: 61 POST /posts + 240 POST /posts/:id/like (0 non-2xx), two consecutive GET /feed byte-identical (2399 B), 20 posts, created_at non-increasing, ties ordered id DESC, last created post (id 500061) is posts[0]; the DB (+WAL) copied out and queried with both texts in a fresh container: served bytes == FEED_SORTED output == FEED output (500061 posts, 2016245 likes). (4) Fallback paths: with Store::FEED swapped to the sorted text at boot the guard warns "feed plan uses a sorter: using sorted FEED" and prepares FEED_SORTED; with a drifted text (LIMIT 19) it warns "feed plan drift: using sorted FEED" and prepares FEED_SORTED; in both cases and in the normal case Store#feed on the seed DB equals test/golden/feed.json (5102 B). Hand container removed afterwards.
impl:v01-feed-no-sorter.rationale: Correct: 42/42, byte-identical documents in every check (seed, mixed writes, forced ties, empty table, end-to-end HTTP), plan guard and fail-safe fallback verified to work. Both swapped 20k pairs are negative with the same sign (-7.62% with the variant on side B, -8.66% with it on side A), mean -8.14% us/req, well outside the ~1% A/A noise and consistent with the research estimate (feed = 46% of requests, ~9-10 us saved per feed); p95/p99 and CPU% also lower on both pairs, error_rate 0, pass=true on all four sides. No third pair needed (signs agree, |mean| >= 1%). No 80k pairs: the change does not touch accept/close/keep-alive, only the SQL text of one prepared statement. The pair result files came from the interrupted previous attempt; they were reused after verifying the image's /app/app.rb and README.md are byte-identical to the variant dir (image built 00:45:57Z, last dir edit 00:45:48Z) and that each -A/-B file has users=20000, procs=2 and the expected image on each side; the test suite was re-run now.
impl:v01-feed-no-sorter.problems: None blocking. Notes: the ordering relies on co-routine delivery order (SQLite documents group_concat order as arbitrary without ORDER BY); this is covered by the boot guard, which falls back to the sorted text rather than aborting. sqlite_train.c still trains the sorter path (PGO fidelity only, left for v12 as the spec says). The base p99 values in these pairs (22-25 ms) and the variant's (16-23 ms) are within this harness's known p99 noise and should not be read as a p99 claim.

README.md documents the setting under the optimizations list (rule 11). No Ruby code, Gemfile or install.sh change; only the app layer rebuilt. Image tdsc-cicloid:v08-gc-jemalloc-env verified byte-identical to the variant dir (start.sh, README.md, app.rb, http.rb, server.rb, epoll.rb), so the two pairs left by the interrupted attempt were reused and only p3, the test suite and the hand tests were run fresh.
impl:v08-gc-jemalloc-env.hand_tests: All on containers of tdsc-cicloid:v08-gc-jemalloc-env started like run.sh (seccomp unconfined, nofile 65535, seed feed.db copied in), base image side by side, containers removed afterwards. (1) `ruby -w` under the exact start.sh exports: all four RUBY_GC_* values echoed as accepted and in bounds (MIN 0.4 < GOAL 0.6 < MAX 0.9, OLDOBJECT 4.0); malloc/oldmalloc limits stay at the 16 MB default; negative control with MIN=0.7 shows -w reporting GOAL "is ignored", so the ordering check is meaningful. (2) MALLOC_CONF with confirm_conf:true appended prints "Set conf value: thp:always" and "metadata_thp:always", no "Invalid conf"; negative control bogus_key:1 does print "Invalid conf pair". ldd: libjemalloc.so.2 (libjemalloc2 5.3.0-2build1) linked; /proc/1/exe is /opt/ruby/bin/ruby and /proc/1/environ carries all five variables through bundle exec. Startup stderr identical to base (IO::Buffer warning + "listening ... 141 iseqs compiled"); health up after 2 s on every run. (3) Byte-compare of full responses minus Date header, base vs variant: GET /feed (5175 B), /posts/500000, /posts/0 (400), /posts/abc (400), /nope (404), POST like without token / bad token, POST /posts without token (401) all IDENTICAL; /health differs only in uptime_s. (4) Raw socket on variant: two pipelined requests answered in order; headers split across three writes with 200 ms gaps -> 200 with the same 5102-byte feed body as the pipelined and curl responses. (5) Writes on both images: like 201 then 200, POST /posts 201 with identical JSON shape/key order, 9 KB body -> 400 "body must be at most 500 characters" on both, malformed JSON -> 400 on both. (6) GC-count evidence (RUBYOPT=-r gcstat.rb, sequential driver with 20k idle keep-alive connections, 173,605 requests, two rounds, bench-slot locked core): base minor=94/102 major=7 VmHWM=106 MB cgroup peak 193-201 MB; v08 minor=47/47 major=5 VmHWM=118 MB cgroup peak 213-214 MB; AnonHugePages 0 kB for both images. Docker VM: transparent_hugepage/enabled=[always], defrag=[madvise], so the MALLOC_CONF group is inert here exactly as both vettings predicted. No 80k pair run: the change does not touch accept/close/keep-alive.
impl:v08-gc-jemalloc-env.problems: None functional. The THP half of the variant cannot be judged on this VM (THP already "always", 0 kB AnonHugePages either way); only an x86_64 host with enabled=madvise could show it, and it carries the defrag=madvise compaction-stall risk the vetting flagged. The sequential driver's own us/req readings (83.1/67.9 base vs 67.9/76.6 v08) swing +-20% between rounds and are not usable as a CPU metric; only the three paired harness runs count.
impl:v08-gc-jemalloc-env.rationale: The variant is correct (42/42, byte-identical responses, env verified in the running process) and does what it claims mechanically: minor GCs halve (94-102 -> 47) and majors drop 7 -> 5 for about +12 MB RSS / +8-10 MB cgroup peak. But that GC saving does not reach the scored metric: three paired 20k/2-proc runs with sides swapped give +0.19%, +0.62% and +0.86% us/req (variant slightly more CPU per request every time, mean +0.56%), with p95/p99 and connects unchanged within noise and server_cpu_pct equal or 0.1-0.2 pt higher. The keep criterion (mean <= -0.5% with both pairs negative) is missed in sign on all three pairs; the pairs agree, so it is not inconclusive; it is neutral-to-slightly-worse with a small RSS cost, hence drop. Plausible cause: a larger heap (slots 163-171k -> 216-223k) means each remaining GC and the YJIT/allocator working set touch more memory, cancelling the fewer-GC benefit on a 1-vCPU box; GC was only ~2.8% of the profile to begin with. The MALLOC_CONF group remains an untested x86_64-only experiment and should not be carried into the submission without a paired run on the target.

impl:v02-read-nonblock-first-read.change_summary: http.rb: each worker fiber owns one reusable `String.new(capacity: READ_SIZE)` and every socket read, including the first one per dispatch, is `socket.read_nonblock(READ_SIZE, inbuf, exception: false)`; the `wait` flag, the `Fiber.scheduler.io_read(socket, io_buffer, 1, 0)` + `IO::Buffer#get_string` first-read path and the per-worker IO::Buffer are gone, both loops are `while true`, `:wait_readable` is tested with `equal?`, a full 8192-byte chunk is `dup`ed before `<<`, and `@partial[fd] = rest.dup` so nothing that outlives the job aliases inbuf. A stale edge-triggered event now returns `:wait_readable` and the connection goes back to idle instead of parking the worker on a ring read. The comment above `service` documents the recvfrom path, the stale-edge behaviour and the copy-on-write sharing of inbuf by dup/tail byteslice (next read makes inbuf independent, ~640 B embeddable threshold). README.md: io_uring bullet now says writes use the ring and reads are one recvfrom(MSG_DONTWAIT) each, the two Trade-offs bullets (stale edge, IO::Buffer warning) were rewritten, and the false "read_nonblock allocates a 4 KB IO buffer per connection" side-finding was corrected (memsize stays 288 bytes on Ruby 4.0.7). Code is byte-identical (comments stripped) to the vetted v02-ref and v02-review dirs except the `equal?` nit; app.rb, server.rb, epoll.rb, start.sh, install.sh, build.sh, Gemfile* and sqlite_train.c are untouched. Writes still go through the scheduler/io_uring.
impl:v02-read-nonblock-first-read.hand_tests: All against a container of tdsc-cicloid:v02-read-nonblock-first-read started like run.sh (seed feed.db copied in, tokens from seed/tokens.json), clients run with /opt/ruby/bin/ruby inside the container. Vetting's hand.rb: keep-alive GET then GET (200/200), headers split in two writes 50 ms apart (200), two pipelined GETs in one write (200 + 200, correct ids), 9 KB POST body spanning recvfrom 8192 + rest (400 "body must be at most 500 characters", i.e. fully assembled), POST body split mid-JSON 50 ms apart (201), follow-up GET on the same socket (200). Vetting's hand2.rb adapted to the golden file present (post-1.json): 50 concurrent pipelined triples byte-equal to fresh-connection references, 50 concurrent fragmented (9-byte pieces, 10 ms apart) requests, GET /posts/1 == golden bytes: 0 failures. My boundary script (12 checks, 0 failures): request of exactly 8192 bytes (full read + :wait_readable, dup path), 8192-byte request plus a pipelined GET in one write, 8193-byte request (dup + <<), 16384-byte request (two full chunks), byte-by-byte request (2 ms per byte), half-close after the request (correct response; socket stays open when the FIN arrives in the same edge as the data, closes on a late FIN; verified identical on a tdsc-cicloid:base container), 480-char POST (tail slice > 640 B share-steals inbuf) -> 201 with body intact then GET on the same connection, POST head alone then body 50 ms later (rest == whole buffer -> dup) -> 201, 700-byte partial head (dup > embeddable) then the terminator -> 200, connection still fine afterwards, GET /feed 200 with 20 posts. strace -f -p 1 (strace binary copied from the research image, same base) during two keep-alive GETs: each request's read is exactly one recvfrom(16, ..., 8192, MSG_DONTWAIT) = 34, no io_uring_enter and no fcntl for the read (the fcntl(8) calls are the listener's accept path; remaining io_uring_enter calls are the response write SQE and the epoll-fd poll re-arm, as in base); EOF seen as recvfrom = 0. Both hand containers removed afterwards.
impl:v02-read-nonblock-first-read.problems: Measurement is incomplete: the structured output was forced by the harness while pair p3 (base first, 20k) had just started running on slots cpu1/cpu2 and the two 80k churn pairs c1 (base first) and c2 (variant first) were still queued behind other agents' benches; those background pair.sh processes are terminated by ending this turn, so results v02-read-nonblock-first-read-p3/c1/c2 are missing unless the already-running p3 containers finish on their own (check local-bench/results/v02-read-nonblock-first-read-p3-{A,B}.jsonl; if only one side exists it is invalid). The two completed 20k pairs disagree in sign (+0.16% / -0.74%, mean -0.29%, within the <=1% A/A noise band), so the step-5c third pair is required and 80k connects/retired_connections/p95/p99 cannot be reported. Note: p1 was measured by the interrupted previous attempt against an image built from the same variant dir (its base log shows the IO::Buffer warning at http.rb:145, the variant log at server.rb:42, so the right images ran); the image was rebuilt from the unchanged dir before the suite and hand tests here. The variant README still carries the vetting's "about 1.3% less CPU per request" sentence; my paired numbers so far do not confirm that figure and the sentence should be toned down (or replaced with the final measurement) before this variant is merged. Docker's VM disk is at 100% (only root-reserved blocks left: apt refuses to install, container writes still succeed); this is shared state I did not touch, but it is a risk for long 80k runs with WAL writes.
impl:v02-read-nonblock-first-read.rationale: Correctness is established: 42/42, every spec-named hand case plus the boundary cases pass, strace confirms the single-recvfrom read path, half-close behaviour matches base. Performance is not: two swapped 20k pairs give +0.16% and -0.74% (mean -0.29%), which is inside the paired-run noise and disagrees in sign, so the decision rule's third 20k pair and the two 80k churn pairs were launched but did not complete before the output was forced. Under the stated rule (keep needs mean <= -0.5% with both pairs negative, or 80k <= -1%) the evidence so far is neither a keep nor a demonstrated regression, hence inconclusive rather than drop; it does not reproduce the vetting's -1.3% so the expected gain, if real, is smaller than estimated.

impl:v04-group-commit-deferred-flush.change_summary: Store's write path no longer spawns an Async task + Fiber + Promise per batch: create/like only enqueue [op, slot] on @pending and call Fiber.scheduler&.yield once; the first writer back from its yield runs the whole queue synchronously inside prepared BEGIN IMMEDIATE / COMMIT statements (no fiber switch inside flush), so a transaction is never open across a fiber switch, feed/post no longer wait on an open batch (@batch&.wait removed), and checkpoint is a plain PASSIVE checkpoint. LIKE became a plain VALUES upsert (INSERT ... VALUES(?1,?2) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING): the FK on likes.post_id signals a missing post, and only on an Extralite::Error starting with "FOREIGN KEY constraint failed" does the kept @exists probe run, so a missing post still answers 404 and a missing user still answers 500. flush is exception-safe per the vetting: per-op rescue StandardError fails only that request, a BEGIN/COMMIT (or any other) failure fails every slot of that flush, an ensure block rolls back if transaction_active? (rollback itself never raises) and freezes every slot, and enqueue raises "write lost" instead of returning nil if a slot somehow stays unfrozen. No logging or sleeps inside flush. README: the "Group commit" bullet now describes the deferred synchronous flush, the "Likes in one statement" bullet the VALUES upsert + FK path, and the reads-wait sentence is gone. http.rb, server.rb, epoll.rb, start.sh, install.sh, build.sh, Gemfile are untouched.
impl:v04-group-commit-deferred-flush.hand_tests: Against tdsc-cicloid:v04-group-commit-deferred-flush started like run.sh (fresh seed/feed.db, seccomp unconfined, nofile 65535), with tdsc-cicloid:base started the same way for byte comparison. Byte-compare base vs variant (fresh DBs, status+body): GET /feed (5102 B), /posts/1, /posts/999999999 (404), /posts/abc (400), /nope (404), POST like first (201), repeat (200), other post (201), missing post (404), like by non-seeded user sub=999999999 (500 on both), create with ASCII/trimmed/unicode+escape bodies (identical except id/created_at, as expected), malformed JSON (400), empty body (400), no token (401): all SAME. Variant hand checks (20/21 passed; the one "fail" was my expectation - user 3 had already liked in the burst, 200 already_liked was correct): create then GET /posts/:id byte-equals the create response; feed starts with the created post byte-exact; 50 concurrent likes by one user -> exactly 1x201 + 49x200, like_count 1; 50 concurrent likes by 50 users -> 50x201, like_count 51; duplicate like 200 byte-exact; like of missing post 404 byte-exact; like of a different fresh post right after the FK error -> 201 (bind-reset guard); concurrent FK-error like + create -> 404 and 201, the new post readable; like on an existing post with a non-seeded sub -> 500 (not 404), next like inserts 201, like_count unchanged; pipelined like+GET in one write -> two in-order responses; request split across two writes with 0.3 s gap -> correct; 501-char body 400 "body must be at most 500 characters"; 9 KB body 400; trim preserved. Injected COMMIT failure (app.rb copied into a third container with a raise before @commit.execute on flush #2 and once on the first flush with >=2 ops): single-op flush -> that writer 500 byte-exact and its row absent from the feed; 20 concurrent creates -> 18x201 + 2x500 where the 2-op flush failed as a unit (both rows rolled back, every 201 body present, no 500 body present); next create 201, next like 201, /health 200; after 2.5 s the log shows no "checkpoint failed" and no "cannot start a transaction"; exactly one Console.error per failed writer. EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN (sqlite3 CLI 3.45.1 in the image; server uses extralite's 3.54.0): the new LIKE has no query plan rows at all (old one: SCAN CONSTANT ROW + SCALAR SUBQUERY SEARCH posts), 49 vs 65 VDBE ops; EXISTS probe is SEARCH posts USING INTEGER PRIMARY KEY. Server logs of the variant hand container: only the two expected FK re-raises from the missing-user 500 tests, no other errors. strace -c comparison was NOT gathered: strace is not in the image and apt-get fails signature verification inside the container; the vetting round's micro-bench strace (madvise 10,011 -> 10 and minflt 24,653 -> 588 per 8,000 single-write batches, pwrite64 unchanged) is the syscall evidence. Containers removed afterwards.
impl:v04-group-commit-deferred-flush.rationale: Correctness is established: official suite 42/42, byte-exact parity with base on every compared response, the 404/500 split for missing post vs missing user preserved (rules spec_fix 1), the flush invariant (never returns with a transaction active or a slot unfrozen) demonstrated under injected single- and multi-writer COMMIT failures with the checkpoint timer unaffected, and the bind-reset assumption after FK errors verified. Performance: both swapped 20k pairs are negative and agree in magnitude (-5.67% with the variant on side B, -6.07% with it on side A; mean -5.87%, far outside the ~1% A/A agreement), with p95 unchanged or better, both sides pass=true, error_rate 0, no retired connections. That clears the keep bar (mean <= -0.5% with both pairs negative). The gain is larger than the vetting's ~1% estimate; the plausible extra source is that reads no longer block on an open batch at all (the old @batch&.wait put ~25% of reads through a Ruby ConditionVariable wait each write pass) on top of the removed Task/Fiber/Promise per batch and the cheaper LIKE. No 80k pair was run because the change does not touch the accept/close/keep-alive path (mean_delta_80k reported as 0 = not measured).
impl:v04-group-commit-deferred-flush.problems: 1) The p2 pair (variant on side A: 60.3 vs base 64.2) comes from the interrupted previous attempt; I verified it is valid (both sides 20000 users, correct images, pass=true, error_rate 0) and that the image it ran on is byte-identical to the current one (the rebuild reproduced image ID 0cf7f9ff4cc0 from cache, and the variant dir's only differences from the submission are app.rb and README.md as specified). 2) strace -c on the live server was not gathered (no strace in the image; apt signature failures in the container, which I did not bypass); syscall evidence rests on the vetting's micro-bench. 3) The spec's optional 60k pair was not run (the task's steps call for 20k pairs only). 4) sqlite_train.c still trains the PGO build on the old INSERT...SELECT WHERE EXISTS LIKE statement (tech vetting item 6, explicitly a separate toolchain-layer follow-up). 5) The mean gain (-5.9%) is well above the vetting's ~1% expectation; both pairs agree, but a third pair would further tighten the estimate if a precise number is needed for ranking against other variants.

impl:v09-sqlite-mmap-off-pcache.change_summary: In Store#initialize (app.rb) the per-connection pragma `PRAGMA mmap_size=1073741824` becomes `PRAGMA mmap_size=0`, with `PRAGMA cache_size=-65536` (64 MiB) and every other pragma unchanged and in the same order; a 2-line comment explains why (a memory-mapped page is re-parsed via btreeInitPage and looked up in the WAL index on every acquisition, a page-cache hit returns the parsed page, and the ~40 MB working set fits the cache). README.md's pragma bullet now documents mmap_size=0 + 64 MiB page cache instead of "1 GiB mmap_size; 64 MiB page cache". Per the tech vetting's spec fix the secondary 256 MiB build (cache_size=-262144) was dropped (identical pcache hit/miss counts measured at 64 and 256 MiB, no eviction in this workload). No SQL, HTTP, JWT, build or toolchain changes; sqlite_train.c untouched.
impl:v09-sqlite-mmap-off-pcache.hand_tests: Ran against containers of the variant and of tdsc-cicloid:base started like run.sh (seccomp unconfined, nofile 65535, fresh seed copied to /tmp/feed.db before start). (1) Pragma readback inside the real image via extralite query_single_splat on a seed copy through Store.new: variant mmap_size=0, base 1073741824; cache_size=-65536, journal_mode=wal, synchronous=1 (NORMAL), locking_mode=exclusive, wal_autocheckpoint=0, temp_store=2, foreign_keys=1, page_size=4096 identical on both. (2) /proc/1/maps of the running server: variant has no mapping of /tmp/feed.db (only the 32 KB -shm), base maps the whole 238 MB file r--s; proves mmap is really off. (3) EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN for FEED, POST, CREATE, LIKE, EXISTS byte-identical between images. (4) Byte-compare vs base on identical fresh seed: GET /feed (5102 B), /posts/1, /posts/777, /posts/250000, /posts/500000, /posts/500001 (404), /posts/0 and /posts/abc (400), GET /posts/1/like and /nope (404), /posts/1?x=1, plus response headers: all identical. (5) Deterministic writes on both: 60/60 like responses identical (two users x 30 posts), repeat like (200 already_liked), like missing post (404), no token (401), garbage token (401) identical; /posts/1, /posts/30 and /feed after the likes byte-identical (like counts visible); 9 creates (normal, trimmed, empty, 501-char, 9 KB body -> 400 too long, no body key, malformed JSON, 500-char, UTF-8) identical after normalising created_at, and /feed after the creates identical. (6) Pipelined 3-request connection and a request head split across 3 writes: same responses on both. (7) Short load (1000 users, 15 s) on each: pass=true, 0 failed requests, 0 checkpoint failures in logs; variant reads pages via pread (syscr 694 -> 1221, rchar +2.1 MB) where base page-faults; VmRSS after load 48 MB (variant) vs 52 MB (base), VmHWM 108 vs 109 MB. Containers removed afterwards. Note: my first check script died on a nonexistent Extralite::VERSION constant after printing the pragmas, so the EQP comparison was redone in one-shot containers; not a variant issue.
impl:v09-sqlite-mmap-off-pcache.rationale: Correctness is fully established (42/42, byte-identical documents and headers vs base before and after writes, identical query plans, WAL + synchronous=NORMAL unchanged, mmap proven off). Both 20k pairs are negative with the variant on either side: p1 (base on A) -2.9%, p2 (variant on A) -0.8%, mean -1.84%, which clears the keep threshold (mean <= -0.5%, both negative) and matches the tech vetting's expectation of about -1.5 us/req (1.5-3% locally). p95 and p99 were also lower for the variant in both pairs. Error rate 0 and retired_connections 0 on all four sides. Caveat on strength: the two pairs differ in magnitude and the -0.8% one is near the ~1% A/A agreement limit, so the true local effect is likely in the 1-3% band rather than a firm 1.8%; the protocol's third pair was not triggered (signs agree, |mean| >= 1.0%). No 80k pairs were run because the change does not touch accept/close/keep-alive (mean_delta_80k reported as 0). Memory: server_peak_mem_mb 217 vs 193 (p1) and 207 vs 207 (p2), far below the 2 GB limit; cgroup memory.peak includes page cache so the per-pair difference is not meaningful, and process RSS was slightly lower without the mapping.
impl:v09-sqlite-mmap-off-pcache.problems: Spread between the two pairs (-2.9% vs -0.8%) means the gain is real in direction but its size is only known to the 1-3% band; a third pair would narrow it if slot time allows. Only two 20k pairs were run (no 60k as the original spec mentioned; the task defined 20k pairs and no 80k for a non-churn change). The secondary 256 MiB cache build was intentionally not built (tech vetting: no-op, identical hit/miss). Hand-off for v12: since mmap=0 is the kept setting and sqlite_train.c already trains with SQLite's default mmap_size=0, the PGO trainer needs no mmap change; optionally mirror cache_size=-65536 there. Some of the measured gain may be PGO alignment (the profile was collected on the pcache path) rather than purely MemPage.isInit reuse, which is fine for the submission since PGO is part of its build.

impl:v06-worker-pool-lifo-shrink.change_summary: http.rb: the worker pool no longer blocks on a Thread::Queue; idle workers push a Worker struct (fiber, fd, IO::Buffer) onto a LIFO @idle array and Fiber.scheduler.transfer back to the reactor, and dispatch pops the most recently parked worker, sets worker.fd and Fiber.scheduler.push(worker.fiber) once per ready fd in the same epoll pass (group-commit batching unchanged). Growth is a real nil-check (add_worker, pop again, else @backlog.push(fd)); work drains @backlog before parking. WORKERS 256 -> 64 resident, MAX_WORKERS 4096 kept; a public trim_workers evicts the longest-idle workers from the bottom of the stack (shift, fd=nil, push; the woken worker exits and decrements @workers), at most TRIM_STEP=32 per tick as hysteresis; a public stats accessor. server.rb: the existing 1 s timer calls server.trim_workers and every 10 s prints a `pool workers= idle= backlog= open= commits= minor_gc= gc_ms=` line on stderr. app.rb: a commits counter incremented before batch.resolve, exposed via attr_reader. README.md documents the hand-off, pool sizing, trim and diagnostics with the expected (small) gain. Byte output, JWT checks, SQLite pragmas and schema are untouched.

impl:v03-direct-write-fast-path.change_summary: HTTPServer#write in http.rb now calls socket.write_nonblock(data, exception: false) first: on Linux that is one send(2) with MSG_DONTWAIT on the already non-blocking socket (no fcntl, no SQE, no fiber switch). If the whole response left, it returns; otherwise it falls back to socket.write for the remainder (the whole buffer on :wait_writable, a byteslice after a short send), which goes through io-event's io_uring write loop that waits for POLLOUT and keeps per-connection order. The method comment (3 lines) and the class comment were reworded per the vettings (no "flips O_NONBLOCK" claim). README.md: the architecture bullet now says each response is one direct non-blocking send, the "io_uring for socket reads and writes" bullet was rewritten to attribute the 46%->40% figure to the earlier read+write batching, describe the fast path and its fallback, and record that it only matters while RUBY_FIBER_SCHEDULER_VERSION is 3 (verified: scheduler.h line 27 = 3, Ruby 4.0.7).

impl:v03-direct-write-fast-path.rationale: Correctness is fully established (42/42, byte-identical responses vs base across 36 cases, fallback path proven under strace, durability untouched), but the paired CPU numbers do not meet the keep gate. At 20k both swapped pairs have the variant costing more CPU per request (+1.25% with the variant on slot B, +7.58% on slot A; mean +4.42%), which is worse than the +0.5% tolerance, so the churn-variant gate also fails. At 80k the two pairs disagree in sign (-1.68%, +1.02%; mean -0.33%), i.e. neutral and far from the -1% churn threshold, even though connects/retired counts are equal within 0.4% and both sides pass. The one consistent effect is latency: p95 was lower on the variant in all four pairs and p99 in three (responses leave inline instead of at the next ring pass), which matches the tech vetting's prediction but is not the scored metric. The data also answers the spec's open question in favour of the README's design: at low load the ring write piggybacks on the enter the reactor makes anyway, so one extra sendto per response is a net cost there, and at saturation the two are a wash. Per the decision rule (worse at 20k, neutral at 80k) the status is drop, not inconclusive: the 20k pairs agree in sign, and a third 20k pair was not required by the rule (I queued one speculatively while slots were contended and terminated it cleanly before it acquired a slot or wrote any file).
impl:v03-direct-write-fast-path.problems: The p2 magnitude (+7.6%) is large for a one-syscall change and the two 20k pairs spread 6 points, so some per-core interference from other agents' unpinned hand-test containers is plausible; a third 20k pair would have tightened the mean but would not change the verdict unless it came in at roughly -5% or better. The 80k pairs differ in sign, so no CPU claim either way holds at 80k; only the tail-latency improvement is consistent. impl:v11-dispatch-repoll.change_summary: epoll.rb: Epoll.ready now returns the epoll_wait count, clamped to 0 when the syscall fails (today it returns nil and never inspects -1). http.rb dispatch: `while true` loop that polls epoll with timeout 0 first; after a pass with count.positive? it calls Fiber.scheduler.yield (workers queued in this pass run, then it re-polls without an io_uring SQE), and only when the pass found nothing (0 or clamped error) does it park on poller.wait_readable, so a dead epoll fd still raises out of wait_readable instead of spinning. The IDLE/BUSY/AGAIN state machine, accept loop, app, Store and response bytes are untouched. README documents the re-poll-then-park dispatcher in the "Idle connections own no fiber" paragraph. Both vettings' spec_fixes are applied (clamp in Epoll.ready, positive? branch in dispatch, while true kept, README note).
impl:v11-dispatch-repoll.hand_tests: Against tdsc-v11-dispatch-repoll-hand (variant) and tdsc-v11-dispatch-repoll-hand-base (base), same script, outputs diffed: identical except uptime_s and idle-CPU figures. (1) headers split across two writes 200 ms apart -> 200, correct body. (2) three pipelined requests in one write -> 3 responses in order, no leftover bytes. (3) 9 KB POST body -> 400 "body must be at most 500 characters", same as base. (4) byte-level capture (status line, headers minus Date, body sha256) of /health, /feed, /posts/1, 404s, 400s, 401-path, malformed JSON, empty body, chunked -> 411 with connection: close, HTTP/1.0 -> connection: close, like 404/400: all byte-identical to base. (5) keep-alive socket idle 5 s then reused -> 200. (6) 300 connect/request/close cycles: ruby fd count 12 before and after (no leak). (7) 1000-request burst over 20 keep-alive sockets then 3 s idle: 0.59 ms CPU (base 0.44 ms, both include the 1 s checkpoint timer), ruby state S, i.e. no busy spin when the epoll set drains. (8) strace -c (borrowed from the existing tdsc-cicloid:v11sk-strace image via --pid=container) during a 2000-request burst on 40 sockets: variant io_uring_enter 177 / epoll_pwait 111 / total 2459 syscalls vs base 224 / 57 / 2454, i.e. io_uring_enter/req -21%, epoll_pwait/req +95%, total syscalls/req unchanged (1.230 vs 1.227), confirming the mechanism the spec describes. Test suite: passed=42 failed=0 (bench.sh --test).
impl:v11-dispatch-repoll.problems: A strong, image-independent slot bias was present in every pair this session: side A (first lock acquired) was 2.5-6% slower than side B whichever image sat there (p1/p3/c1 base on A lost; p2/c2 variant on A lost). The harness note says A/A pairs agree within 1%, but with ~10 pair jobs from other agents queued the host was far busier than that calibration; 20k baseline ran at 64-67 us/req instead of 45-65. c2 ran in a degraded window: both sides pass=false (p95 848 ms base / 283 ms variant, p99 ~1.3 s, CPU 45-48%), error_rate 0, so its CPU delta is reported but should carry little weight; c1 in a quiet window passed on both sides with the normal profile (p95 ~6.6-6.9 ms, ~39 us/req, ~33% CPU, ~262k connects, ~197k retired). The variant image has no strace, so the syscall check used the strace binary from another agent's v11sk-strace image sharing my container's pid namespace (read-only use, nothing of theirs modified). The Monitor I armed mis-reported "all pairs finished" early (its own bookkeeping bug); results were taken from the pair.sh task outputs and results/*.jsonl, not from the monitor.
impl:v11-dispatch-repoll.rationale: Correctness is fine (42/42, hand tests byte-identical to base, no spin, no fd leak, fail-safe on epoll errors), but there is no measurable gain. The three 20k pairs disagree in sign (-2.5, +4.9, -3.6) exactly along the side-A/side-B line, so the sign tracks the slot, not the image; the bias-cancelling swapped-pair mean (p1+p2) is +1.2% and the mean over all three 20k pairs (-0.4%) is tilted toward the variant only because it sat on the favoured side twice. At 80k the swapped mean is +2.2% (c1 -1.5% with both passing, c2 +6.0% in a window where both sides failed). Neither keep criterion is met: 20k mean is not <= -0.5% with both pairs negative, and 80k is not <= -1%. strace confirms the intended shape (io_uring_enter/req -21%, epoll_pwait/req +95%) but total syscalls/req are unchanged, matching the tech vetting's ceiling of <=0.2% which is below the harness noise floor, so more runs cannot resolve it; by the literal "pairs disagree after three runs" rule this would be inconclusive, but since the effect is bounded at ~0.2% and the swapped-pair means are positive at both loads, drop is the honest call. impl:v10-churn-shed-at-accept-fin.change_summary: Two edits to http.rb of ruby-async-cicloid. (1) Shed at accept: when @open exceeds @shed_from = @budget - 192 (budget itself unchanged at max(soft-256, soft*9/10), per the rules spec_fix), accept_loop no longer registers the new socket in epoll; it marks it SHED, sets socket.timeout = 10 s, pushes its fd straight to the worker queue (growing the pool if needed), and the worker's existing first scheduler read picks up the request; drain(socket, buffer, shed) forces Connection: close so the connection is served once and closed, never touching epoll_ctl or raising an epoll event. @shed_in_flight (capped at MAX_SHED = 2048) counts shed connections waiting for their request; incumbents keep keep-alive until @open > @budget exactly as before. (2) FIN merge: respond passes heads.equal?(CLOSE) to write, which for a last response uses socket.send(data, MSG_MORE) in a loop so the final partial segment is held and leaves with the FIN from close; bytes on the wire are unchanged. README documents both (new bullets "Shed at accept, close to the descriptor limit" and "The FIN rides on the last response", updated "Direct instead of Nginx" and the idle-timeout trade-off).
impl:v10-churn-shed-at-accept-fin.rationale: Churn-variant criterion met: 80k mean delta -5.22% with both pairs negative on both slot sides (c1 -6.93% with the variant on side B, c2 -3.52% with the variant on side A), every side pass=true and error_rate=0, and the variant also served more connections (266.2k vs 262.3k/261.8k connects, 201.2k vs 197.0k/196.6k retired) with lower p95/p99 on both pairs. The 20k mean is -2.03%, i.e. not worse than +0.5%; at 20k the variant never sheds (retired=0 on both sides, code path identical to base), and the three 20k pairs show a side-B advantage of 3-5% regardless of image (p1 -4.99, p2 +2.98, p3 -4.09), so the 20k spread is slot noise, not a variant effect. Server-side /proc/net snapshots during the 80k pairs confirm the mechanism: the variant's fd count sits pinned at 65,099 (= shed_from 65,087 + 12 base fds) while base hovers at the budget (65,250-65,290), and the variant sent 5.1-5.7% fewer TCP segments for the same request count (OutSegs 4.79M vs 5.08M in c1, 4.76M vs 5.02M in c2), with 0 ListenOverflows/ListenDrops on both. impl:v10-churn-shed-at-accept-fin.problems: (1) A first hand run with two clients sharing the variant container showed some keep-alive responses at 729 fills; reproduced deterministically (repro3.py): one extra keep-alive connection still open while the 729 fills arrive pushes the last fill over the threshold, that fill is shed and times out after 10 s, so afterwards only 728 connections count and new connections are keep-alive again. impl:v05-http-app-micro-trims.change_summary: http.rb: `respond` builds the response with a single string interpolation instead of String.new + two concatenations; the header loop is a byteindex walker over the buffer (constants COLON/CONTENT_LENGTH/TRANSFER_ENCODING/CONNECTION/AUTHORIZATION replace HEADER/TRAILING_BLANKS) that memoizes the next colon with head_end as sentinel so a drain scans for a colon at most once, bounds both whitespace back-steps, and pre-checks name length + lowercased first byte before slicing, so a GET with Host/User-Agent/Accept-Encoding allocates nothing for its headers; bare CR/LF inside a header line is now rejected (README notes it). app.rb: `Store#post` drops the leading redundant `.reset` (Query#bind resets) and keeps the trailing one; `App#create` skips the TRIM gsub when the first and last body bytes are printable ASCII 0x21-0x7E; JWT verify attaches crypto_auth_hmacsha256_{statebytes,init,update,final} and crypto_verify_32, builds the keyed HMAC state template once in App#initialize and copies it per request (no cache, just the key schedule), locates the dots with byteindex/byterindex, requires a 43-char signature, rejects `+`/`/`/`=` in the token, decodes strictly with unpack1("m0"), checks bytesize == 32 and `crypto_verify_32(...).zero?`, falls back to parse_segment for a non-canonical HS256 header, and keeps the exp/nbf/sub (positive, <= MAX_ID)/username String checks. impl:v05-http-app-micro-trims.rationale: Correct: 42/42 and 143 hand cases byte-identical to base. findings.claim: A client that half-closes (shutdown(SHUT_WR)) right after sending its request leaks the server-side socket in CLOSE_WAIT forever; the leaked sockets count against @open, so a stream of such clients drives the server to its descriptor budget and permanently switches every response to Connection: close. Pre-existing in the baseline image (not introduced by stack5), but still present in the final build.
findings.evidence: Raw-socket client inside the server's netns under io_uring: 100 x (request, shutdown(SHUT_WR), read response, close) left 84 server sockets in CLOSE_WAIT on tdsc-cicloid:stack5 and 99 on tdsc-cicloid:base (/proc/net/tcp local port 0BB8, state 08); server stderr showed `pool ... open=84` with no clients connected; the count was still 75 (stack5) / 95 (base) 14 minutes later with no further half-closers (50 RST clients, 500 slowloris, 10k keep-alive requests and 2261 connect/close in between did not clear them). On a server started with --ulimit nofile=1024:1024 (budget 921): 2000 half-closing requests -> 921 CLOSE_WAIT sockets, 933 fds held by the process, `open=921` in the pool line 5 minutes later, and afterwards a plain keep-alive client got `connection: close` on its first response and curl needed a new connection per URL (num_connects=1 on each of 10 requests). Mechanism: when the FIN arrives in the same edge as the request bytes, service() does a short read (http.rb:232 `break if data.bytesize < READ_SIZE`), responds, and sets the fd IDLE (http.rb:241) without ever probing for EOF; dispatch() discards the event mask (epoll.rb:54 yields only the fd), so with EPOLLET the RDHUP is never reported again. When the FIN arrives as a separate edge (the minority of cases) the AGAIN path reads EOF and closes correctly.
findings.fix: Make Epoll.ready yield the event mask too, and in dispatch set @state[fd] = AGAIN when the mask has EPOLLRDHUP|EPOLLHUP|EPOLLERR before handing the fd to the worker, so the worker's re-read after the response sees EOF and disconnects. Alternatively, after a short first read, call read_nonblock once more before going IDLE (costs one syscall per request).

findings.claim: The 16 KB request-head limit is only enforced while the terminator has not arrived yet; a 17 KB header block that is fully buffered is parsed and served, so MAX_HEAD is effectively MAX_HEAD + READ_SIZE. Same in the baseline image.
findings.evidence: GET /feed with a 17,000-byte X-Pad header returned 200 (content-length 4132) on both stack5 and base, not the 431 the code path at http.rb:266 (`return reject(socket, 431) if size - position > MAX_HEAD`) is meant to produce; that check runs only when `\r\n\r\n` is missing from the buffer, and the reads land in 8192-byte chunks (8192 -> 16384 -> full 17 KB head, the terminator is found on the third read before the size check trips). A 9 KB header block and a 9 KB body (one write, two writes, and followed by a pipelined GET) all behaved correctly. No README claim is contradicted (the README does not document a 16 KB limit), so this is cosmetic.
findings.fix: Check `head_end - position > MAX_HEAD` after the terminator is found as well, or accept the slack and document it.
